![Pug Unit Frames: the pug emblem and the name over a party of four, the player casting, a hostile target and a corner of a raid, in a forge hall where a dwarf stands with his hammer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skytruax/PugUnitFrames/main/docs/banner.png)

# Pug Unit Frames

  **Clean, light unit frames for World of Warcraft: Forever.**

  You, your target and its target, focus, pet, party and raid: dark, thin and easy to read.

  A pug is a small dog, and a PUG is a pick-up group. These are frames for both.

  [![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/skytruax/PugUnitFrames?label=release&color=d9a441)](https://github.com/skytruax/PugUnitFrames/releases/latest)
  [![Tests](https://github.com/skytruax/PugUnitFrames/actions/workflows/tests.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/skytruax/PugUnitFrames/actions/workflows/tests.yml)
  ![World of Warcraft: Forever 1.60.1](https://img.shields.io/badge/WoW%20Forever-1.60.1-3b82c4)
  [![Licence: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-MIT-3fa55b)](https://github.com/skytruax/PugUnitFrames/blob/main/LICENSE)

  [Install](#install) ·
  [What you get](#what-you-get) ·
  [Settings](#settings) ·
  [How it is built](#how-it-is-built) ·
  [Developing](#developing)

  ![A fight on the frames, moment by moment: the pull, the tank taking the hits, a party member poisoned while the player heals, the heal landing as a cast is interrupted, and the target nearly dead](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skytruax/PugUnitFrames/main/docs/demo.gif)

The moving picture is the addon's own code drawing a fight in a simulator of the game's interface, over a
painted city ([how](#developing)). The picture at the top is an illustration built from the addon's own artwork.
Neither is a screenshot of the game. The spell icons, raid marks, portraits and the dragon beside an elite's level are
Blizzard's (the portraits are the faces the game shows until it has drawn a unit's own), and the title lettering is
LifeCraft, a typeface by Eliot Truelove.

---

## A homage, not the original

[PitBull Unit Frames 4.0](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/pitbull-unit-frames-4-0), by
ckknight, shefkin and nebula169 ([source](https://github.com/nebularg/PitBull4)), is the dog-themed
unit frames addon a great many of us played with for years, and the credit for the idea belongs to
them. PitBull has not come to Forever, so here is a smaller dog in its honour.

Pug Unit Frames is **not that project** and has nothing to do with its authors. It is a new addon,
written from scratch, with none of PitBull's code or art in it. Until version 0.2 it was called
Free Unit Frames.

## Status

**0.3 changes what you see when you log in**: first name and surname, portraits, a dragon on
elites, Questie's quest icons, and a party with its buffs above each member
([changelog](https://github.com/skytruax/PugUnitFrames/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)). It passes both of its test suites (a model of the client that seals
values the way the game does, and a simulator running Blizzard's real interface code). Neither is
the game, so expect a rough edge. If something looks wrong in the game, `/pug status` lists any
error it caught: please open an issue with that text.

## What you get

  

    

      ![A game screen with all seven frames labelled: raid, party, focus, pet, player, target, target of target](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skytruax/PugUnitFrames/main/curseforge/web/02-frames.jpg)
      **Seven frames, yours to arrange.** Player, target, target of target, focus, pet, party,
      and raid for 10, 20 or 40. Each can be switched off, sized, scaled and moved on its own.
    

    

      ![Party frames with a threat outline, incoming heal, removable debuff and range fade, beside a raid of twenty](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skytruax/PugUnitFrames/main/curseforge/web/03-groups.jpg)
      **Your group, at a glance.** An outline on whoever is being attacked, healing on its way
      past the end of the bar, a frame lit in the colour of a debuff you can remove, and members
      out of range faded.
    

  

  

    

      ![A checklist of what keeps working in a fight, beside a hostile target with debuffs, a threat outline and a shielded cast bar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skytruax/PugUnitFrames/main/curseforge/web/04-combat.jpg)
      **Built for how Forever fights.** In a fight the game seals health, names, casts and auras
      from addons. These frames are written around that, and a late joiner gets a frame at once.
    

    

      ![Debuff icons rimmed by kind, three cast bars, and the four places icons can go](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skytruax/PugUnitFrames/main/curseforge/web/05-auras.jpg)
      **Buffs, debuffs and cast bars.** Icons with time left and stacks, debuffs rimmed in the
      colour of their kind, on the target only your own if you like. Cast bars with a shield on a
      cast that cannot be interrupted, which on the target and the focus is a grey orange and not
      the cast's gold, and a moment of red when a cast is interrupted.
    

  

  

    

      ![The same frames in the themes Slate, Night and Hearth, with smooth, flat and glass bars](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skytruax/PugUnitFrames/main/curseforge/web/06-looks.jpg)
      **Three looks, three textures.** Slate, Night and Hearth, all drawn for this addon, lettered
      in Inter (which the addon brings with it; the game's own font is one setting away), with a
      soft shadow under every plate if you like one. Health coloured by class, by friend or foe, by
      how much is left, or plain; numbers exact, short, as a percentage, or as what is missing.
    

    

      ![Green handles on the frames of a game screen, one being dragged, and the list of commands](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skytruax/PugUnitFrames/main/curseforge/web/07-arrange.jpg)
      **Unlock, drag, done.** A handle on every frame, and everything else in the options, frame
      by frame. Profiles can be copied, switched per character, and carried in and out as text.
    

  

Also in there: portraits; a character's first name and surname, on a line of their own wherever a
frame has the height (first name over surname on a raid frame), which is also where a long creature
name fits; the game's dragon beside the level of an elite or rare creature (and the level on a
small badge at the foot of the portrait, for those who switch that on); Questie's icon on a
creature that one of your quests needs, if you run [Questie](https://github.com/Questie/Questie);
each party member's buffs in a row above the frame, as on the target; raid icons, resting, in
combat, ready-check answers and a resurrection on its way; the leader's crown, a mark for tank,
healer and damage and a flag on anyone marked for fighting players, each of them switched on if you
want it; shields drawn after the health as healing on its way is, with a pale cap on the end of
the bar when there is more shield than room; combo points on the target for rogues and
druids, a druid's mana under the form's bar, a hunter's pet's mood, and totems under the player for
shamans, sent away with a right click; party frames when you are alone, if you like to see yourself
there, in order of role if you like; a player frame that fades when nothing is going on; English,
German, Spanish and French.

A click on a frame targets the unit, with Shift, Ctrl or Alt held as well, and a right click opens
its menu. The game's ping key pings whoever a frame shows. Addons that bind spells to clicks on
unit frames find these frames where they look for them. With a controller, the menu the game opens
on your target works as it does without the addon: the game's own target frame, which that menu
belongs to, is set aside unseen and not hidden.

These six pictures are illustrations, not screenshots, drawn by `tools/make_listing.py`
from the addon's own textures and layout numbers, as the frames look since version 0.3. The spell icons,
raid marks, portraits and the elite dragon in them are Blizzard's.

## Install

1. Download the zip from the [latest release](https://github.com/skytruax/PugUnitFrames/releases/latest).
2. Unzip it into `World of Warcraft\_forever_\Interface\AddOns\`, so that you end up with
   `...\AddOns\PugUnitFrames\PugUnitFrames.toc`.
3. Start the game, or log out and in again if it is running.

The game's own player, target, focus, pet, party and raid frames and its cast bar step aside for the
ones this addon draws. Each can be kept: Options > AddOns > Pug Unit Frames. The raid frames start
switched off, so in a raid you have the game's own until you switch these on (Options > Frames >
Raid > Show this frame).

## Settings

`/pug` opens the options.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/pug` | open the options |
| `/pug unlock` | show a green box on every frame; drag one to move its frame |
| `/pug lock` | put the boxes away |
| `/pug reset <frame\|all>` | put a frame back where and how it started (`player`, `target`, `targettarget`, `focus`, `pet`, `party`, `raid`) |
| `/pug profile` | your settings as text to copy; paste someone else's to bring them in as a new profile |
| `/pug status` | version, what the game is sealing right now, and any errors caught this session |

Frames are protected by the game while you fight: they can be moved, sized, switched on and off only
out of combat. A change made in a fight is kept and happens when the fight ends.

## How it is built

On this client much of what a unit frame shows reaches an addon **sealed**: the game hands over a
value that can be passed on to be drawn, and that the addon may not read, compare or calculate with.
Health always is. Maximum health, power, names, classes, casts, auras, threat and range are under
conditions Blizzard documents.

Pug Unit Frames is written so that it never needs to know. Every such value goes straight from the
game function that answers it to a widget method that Blizzard documents as accepting sealed
values: a bar's value, a text, a texture, an alpha. Where something has to be decided on a number
the addon cannot see (which threat outline? how many combo points?), the deciding is given to the
game too: a row of bars, each running from one level to the next, which the game fills.

All of that lives in one file, [`Sealed.lua`](https://github.com/skytruax/PugUnitFrames/blob/main/PugUnitFrames/Sealed.lua), and the test suite fails
if any other file calls a game function whose answer can be sealed. The list of those functions is
made from Blizzard's own API documentation.

Buffs and debuffs are the exception, because for them there is no sealed answer to pass on: while
the game keeps auras sealed, an addon that so much as asks which auras a unit has gets an error.
What the game offers instead is its own aura container, a frame an addon creates and sets up (which
unit, which auras, how many, in what rows) and the game fills itself. This addon gives each of the
container's buttons its parts as the game creates it (an icon, a sweep for the time left, a count,
a rim) and never learns what any aura is. [`Elements/Auras.lua`](https://github.com/skytruax/PugUnitFrames/blob/main/PugUnitFrames/Elements/Auras.lua)
is all of it.

The frames are the game's secure unit buttons, and party and raid are its secure group headers, so
they keep working in combat, including for someone who joins in the middle of a fight. No library
and no other addon's code is included, the game's menus are left alone, and none of its code is
hooked. The game's own frames are put away as the addon loads, before any of them has come up, so
that none of their code runs on the addon's account: on this client that is what keeps protected
actions, a controller's among them, from being refused later.

## Developing

```
PugUnitFrames/        the addon: what goes into Interface/AddOns
  Sealed.lua           the one place that touches values the game can seal
  Frame.lua            the plate, the events, and the layout every frame shares
  Elements/            one file per thing a frame shows
  Units.lua Group.lua  the single frames; the party and raid headers
tools/
  tests/               the model of the client and the scenarios run against it
  sim/                 the simulator run: Blizzard's real interface code, in Docker
    run.sh demo.sh     the tests and the picture; the moving demo
    menu.sh            opens the target's menu the way the game's controller mode does
    photos.sh          the picture over photographs of your own, each marked as a composite
    scene_art.py       what a picture needs that the simulator lacks: icons, raid marks, portraits, a world, the font
  make_art.py          draws every texture the addon ships
  make_listing.py      draws the banner, the logo and the store pictures
  forge_hall.py        the dwarf in his forge hall behind the title pictures: a drawing of our own
  game_icons.py        fetches the game's own spell icons, raid marks, portraits and dragons those pictures show
  brand.py             the look those pictures share with FreeControl's
  sealed_list.py       makes tools/sealed_apis.txt from Blizzard's API documentation
```

Two test suites, neither needing the game:

```
pip install lupa==2.8
python3 tools/tests/run.py           # a model of the client that seals values; also checks the source
tools/sim/lab/build-image.sh         # once: fetches the simulator and builds its Docker image
tools/sim/run.sh                     # Blizzard's interface code with the addon loaded; takes a picture
tools/sim/menu.sh                    # the controller's menu on the target: does it stay open?
tools/sim/demo.sh                    # the same fight, moment by moment: docs/demo.gif
tools/sim/photos.sh                  # the same fight over pictures of your own (tools/sim/backdrops/)
```

Neither is the game. The model is written from Blizzard's documentation and the simulator does not
seal values, so anything that depends on how the live client behaves is confirmed by playing.

  ![The frames as the simulator draws them in the middle of a fight: a party of four with a threat outline, a removable debuff and a member out of range, a focus casting, the player healing, and a hostile elite target with its debuffs and a cast that cannot be interrupted](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skytruax/PugUnitFrames/main/docs/sim-screenshot.png)

The addon's own code drawing beside Blizzard's interface code in the simulator. The simulator has
none of the game's art and no world, and reads no font from an addon's folder, so the scene
(`tools/sim/tests/sim/screenshot.lua`) hands it the game's icons for its spells, the raid marks, the game's stand-in
portraits and its elite dragon, a painted city and the addon's own font, and answers the game functions the simulator has no handle for: other units' casts
and power, threat, range. The simulator knows no auras for the scene's people either, so the scene puts them on the addon's buttons itself, in the rows the game's
aura container lays them in. Blizzard's own interface, bare without its art, is put away.

The pictures and textures are drawn by scripts too (`pip install pillow numpy`):

```
python3 tools/make_art.py            # the textures in PugUnitFrames/Art
python3 tools/make_listing.py        # docs/banner.png, docs/social.png, the logo, curseforge/gallery
```

The pictures show the game's own spell icons, raid marks, stand-in portraits and elite dragon, as the
frames show the game's art in the game. Those
are Blizzard Entertainment's and are not part of this repository: `tools/game_icons.py` fetches
them into a git-ignored folder from a [public mirror](https://github.com/Gethe/wow-ui-textures) of
the game's interface art when the pictures are built (`--placeholders` draws stand-ins instead).
The addon itself ships no icon: it hands whatever the game names back to the game to draw.

## Licence

MIT. See [LICENSE](https://github.com/skytruax/PugUnitFrames/blob/main/LICENSE).

The addon brings one thing that is not ours: the typeface its frames are lettered in,
[Inter](https://github.com/rsms/inter) by the Inter Project Authors, under the SIL Open Font
License 1.1. The font file is unchanged and its licence is beside it
([PugUnitFrames/Fonts](https://github.com/skytruax/PugUnitFrames/blob/main/PugUnitFrames/Fonts)).

The simulator the tests use is a separate project under GPL-3.0
([wow-ui-sim](https://github.com/Osso/wow-ui-sim)); nothing of it is part of the addon.

releases.notes:
# Changelog

## v0.3.5

New:

- **A cast that cannot be interrupted is a grey orange.** On the cast bar of your target and of your focus, a cast that cannot be interrupted is drawn in a greyed orange in place of the cast's gold, so you see before you reach for an interrupt whether it would do anything. The shield on the end of the bar is still there, and the colour changes with it if a cast becomes interruptible part-way. "Grey orange if uninterruptible" is a setting of each frame's cast bar (Options > Frames > Bars): it starts on for target and focus, and off for player, pet and party.

Fixed:

- **A pale strip on the end of every health bar.** The cap that says "more shield than there is room for" stood on every health bar, shield or no shield, a dead creature's included. It is drawn only while the unit has a shield and the shield does not all fit, which is what it was made for. It is one even colour now, without the fade it had.
- **The addon's font.** Whether the game takes the addon's font file was decided on a piece of text nobody sees, and in the game the answer was no for a whole evening: every text stayed in the game's font, and ten minutes in it was called an error. Each text is now given the game's font and then the addon's on top of it, so a text carries the addon's font from the moment the game takes it there, and keeps the game's where it does not.
- A font the game does not take is no longer listed as an error, and the game is no longer asked for it on a timer all evening: a few times as the frames are made, once more a little later, and after that only when frames are laid out again. The "Font" line of `/pug status` says how many texts carry the addon's font, whether the game knows the file, and what it answered.

Good to know:

- If your frames are lettered in the game's font and you would like the addon's: close the game completely and start it again. This game works with the files that were in an addon's folder when it was started, and a font file that was installed or updated while it was running may not be taken until then. A reload does not change that.

## v0.3.4

- **New starting settings.** A new profile, and a frame you reset, now starts with the settings the addon's author plays with:
    - larger frames (player and target at 115%, party at 120%, focus at 130%), with a taller power bar and cast bar on player and target;
    - health written as an amount on player, target and party;
    - cast bars and levels on the party, and party portraits that look towards the bars;
    - at most six buffs on the target, and no raid mark or combat mark on it;
    - no shadows under the frames;
    - raid frames switched off: in a raid you keep the game's own raid frames until you switch these on (Options > Frames > Raid > Show this frame).
- **Where the frames start.** On a wide screen (an interface scaled down, or an ultrawide monitor) they start in the author's arrangement: player at the left and target at the right of the fight, focus and pet out at the left edge, the party below the player. Where that does not fit, they start close together around the lower middle, as before, moved apart a little for their new sizes.
- **Settings you already have are not changed**: no frame of yours is moved, resized or switched off by this update. `/pug reset all` gives you the new starting settings if you want them.

## v0.3.3

- **The level is plain text again**, at the start of the line under the name with the dragon before it, exactly as it was before 0.3.2. The badge that 0.3.2 put on the portrait is still there for those who liked it, as a setting that starts switched off: "Level as a badge", Options > Frames > Text and portrait. Settings saved by 0.3.2 have it switched off once, since 0.3.2 had switched it on for everyone; if you want the badge, switch it on again.

Fixed, after a second reading of 0.3.2:

- Logging in or reloading in the middle of a fight, with the game slow to hand the addon's font over: the frames made when the fight ended were lettered in the game's font, while `/pug status` said the addon's was in use. They are made in the font the game has handed over by then.
- With the font set to the game's own, the addon's font file was still tried, and reported after ten minutes if the game would not take it. A font nobody asks for is left alone.
- Icons on the target of target (off unless you switch them on) were taken down and put up again four times a second, and the tooltip of the one under the mouse with them. Once a second now.
- A part of a frame that could not be made was made again at every change of a setting, each time leaving its pieces behind. It is tried once.
- The level's badge, on a frame without a portrait and with a low health bar, could hang a pixel over the bar's lower edge.

## v0.3.2

Fixed:

- **Buffs and debuffs in a fight.** In a fight this game does not let an addon ask which buffs and debuffs a unit has: every such question is an error (the line "Auras cannot be accessed when secret" in `/pug status`, hundreds of times in an evening), and the icons stood still until the fight was over. The icons are now drawn by the game's own aura container, which the game fills itself, in a fight and out of it, on buttons this addon dresses: icon, time left, stacks, and a rim in the colour of the debuff's kind. The light on a party or raid frame for a debuff you can remove works the same way. The tooltip on an icon is the game's own.
- **The addon's font.** The game can take its time before it hands an addon's font file over. Version 0.3.1 gave up after twelve seconds, lettered the frames in the game's font for the rest of the session and called it an error. The file is now asked for as the addon loads and tried again for as long as it takes, and the frames change to it the moment the game takes it. Only after ten minutes of refusals is anything said, once. `/pug status` has a "Font" line that says which font is in use and why.
- One part of a frame that fails no longer keeps the rest of that frame, or the frames laid out after it, from being set up; it is reported and left out.

New:

- **The level on a badge.** The player's and the target's level stands on a small dark tile at the foot of the portrait, the number and the rim in the colour of how hard the fight would be, gold for someone who cannot be fought. An elite's dragon and a rare creature's star are inside it, and the number then stands alone. On a frame without a portrait the badge starts the line the level was on. "Level as a badge" is a setting of each frame (Options > Frames > Text and portrait) and starts switched on; off, the level is plain text as before.

Good to know:

- Icons come in the game's order now, your own first.
- A change to the icons' size made in the middle of a fight is taken up when the fight ends: the game closes its aura buttons to addons while it keeps auras sealed.

## v0.3.1

- **Shields are drawn the way healing on its way is**: a pale stretch of bar that starts where the health ends (after the healing, when some is on its way) and is as long as the shield is large. It takes the place of the band along the top of the bar. Only as much of a shield is drawn as there is room for before the end of the bar; when there is more shield than room, a pale cap lights up on the bar's end. That cap is all a shield on someone at full health has to show, which is when a shield is usually cast. "Shields on the health bar" still switches it, frame by frame.

## v0.3.0

What you see when you log in has changed. Every part of it is a setting, and can be switched back.

# Changelog

## v0.3.3

- **The level is plain text again**, at the start of the line under the name with the dragon before it, exactly as it was before 0.3.2. The badge that 0.3.2 put on the portrait is still there for those who liked it, as a setting that starts switched off: "Level as a badge", Options > Frames > Text and portrait. Settings saved by 0.3.2 have it switched off once, since 0.3.2 had switched it on for everyone; if you want the badge, switch it on again.

Fixed, after a second reading of 0.3.2:

- Logging in or reloading in the middle of a fight, with the game slow to hand the addon's font over: the frames made when the fight ended were lettered in the game's font, while `/pug status` said the addon's was in use. They are made in the font the game has handed over by then.
- With the font set to the game's own, the addon's font file was still tried, and reported after ten minutes if the game would not take it. A font nobody asks for is left alone.
- Icons on the target of target (off unless you switch them on) were taken down and put up again four times a second, and the tooltip of the one under the mouse with them. Once a second now.
- A part of a frame that could not be made was made again at every change of a setting, each time leaving its pieces behind. It is tried once.
- The level's badge, on a frame without a portrait and with a low health bar, could hang a pixel over the bar's lower edge.

## v0.3.2

Fixed:

- **Buffs and debuffs in a fight.** In a fight this game does not let an addon ask which buffs and debuffs a unit has: every such question is an error (the line "Auras cannot be accessed when secret" in `/pug status`, hundreds of times in an evening), and the icons stood still until the fight was over. The icons are now drawn by the game's own aura container, which the game fills itself, in a fight and out of it, on buttons this addon dresses: icon, time left, stacks, and a rim in the colour of the debuff's kind. The light on a party or raid frame for a debuff you can remove works the same way. The tooltip on an icon is the game's own.
- **The addon's font.** The game can take its time before it hands an addon's font file over. Version 0.3.1 gave up after twelve seconds, lettered the frames in the game's font for the rest of the session and called it an error. The file is now asked for as the addon loads and tried again for as long as it takes, and the frames change to it the moment the game takes it. Only after ten minutes of refusals is anything said, once. `/pug status` has a "Font" line that says which font is in use and why.
- One part of a frame that fails no longer keeps the rest of that frame, or the frames laid out after it, from being set up; it is reported and left out.

New:

- **The level on a badge.** The player's and the target's level stands on a small dark tile at the foot of the portrait, the number and the rim in the colour of how hard the fight would be, gold for someone who cannot be fought. An elite's dragon and a rare creature's star are inside it, and the number then stands alone. On a frame without a portrait the badge starts the line the level was on. "Level as a badge" is a setting of each frame (Options > Frames > Text and portrait) and starts switched on; off, the level is plain text as before.

Good to know:

- Icons come in the game's order now, your own first.
- A change to the icons' size made in the middle of a fight is taken up when the fight ends: the game closes its aura buttons to addons while it keeps auras sealed.

## v0.3.1

- **Shields are drawn the way healing on its way is**: a pale stretch of bar that starts where the health ends (after the healing, when some is on its way) and is as long as the shield is large. It takes the place of the band along the top of the bar. Only as much of a shield is drawn as there is room for before the end of the bar; when there is more shield than room, a pale cap lights up on the bar's end. That cap is all a shield on someone at full health has to show, which is when a shield is usually cast. "Shields on the health bar" still switches it, frame by frame.

## v0.3.0

What you see when you log in has changed. Every part of it is a setting, and can be switched back.

- **First name and surname.** A character on Forever has both, and the frames wrote only the first. They write both now, as the game's own frames do. On a raid frame the surname has a line of its own under the first name. If you have the game hide your own surname, your own frame leaves it off as well. "Surname" is a setting of each frame.
- **Room for a whole name.** Where a frame has the height, the name has a line to itself, as wide as the health bar, with the level and the health number on the line under it and the power number on the power bar. A long creature name is written out where it used to be cut short, and the party frame starts wider so that two names of twelve letters fit beside a portrait.
- **Portraits** on the player, the target (at the right end, as the game has it), the focus and each party member. Options > Frames > Text and portrait.
- **A dragon beside the level of an elite or rare creature**: the game's own, as on its nameplates. Gold for an elite or a boss, silver for a rare elite, a star for a rare creature. The "+" and "R" after the level stay.
- **Questie's quest icon.** A creature that one of your quests needs carries the icon Questie puts on its nameplate, in the top right corner of the target, target of target and focus frames. It needs Questie to be installed. In a dungeon the game does not tell addons which creature a unit is, and there is no icon there.
- **The leader's mark, the role mark and the PvP flag start switched off**, and each has its own setting now (Options > Frames > Marks). Raid icons, resting, in combat and ready-check answers are as before.
- **Party: buffs above each member**, in a row as on the target, with the debuffs still beside the frame; and health written as an amount, not a percentage.
- Buffs and debuffs each have their own side of a frame ("Buffs go", "Debuffs go"), in place of one setting for both.
- The members of a group stand apart by the gap you set plus whatever stands between them (a row of icons, a cast bar), so one member's icons no longer lie on the next member's frame. A gap you had set by hand is taken down by what stood between the frames, so they stay as far apart as you had them.
- The target of target starts wider and without a health number, so that a name fits on it; the focus frame starts larger, with room for a portrait and a long name.
- On a frame with two lines of text a raid mark sits at the end of the name's line, clear of the name and of the icons above the frame, and the small marks on the frame's top edge stand over its portrait, clear of where the name begins.
- The frame settings have a fifth section, Marks.

Your settings: a setting you had never changed moves to its new starting value, and whatever you had chosen stays as you chose it. A party whose icons you had set up keeps them exactly as they were. There is no telling a setting left alone from one set to the same value on purpose, so if you had, say, kept portraits off deliberately, switch them off once more. Profile text exported from 0.2 can still be pasted in.

## v0.2.0

- A new name: Pug Unit Frames. It was Free Unit Frames, a name that turned out to be in use already. A pug is a small dog, and a PUG is a pick-up group. It is a homage to PitBull Unit Frames, which has not come to Forever, and it is not that project.
- The addon's folder is now `PugUnitFrames` and its command `/pug` (also `/puf` and `/pugunitframes`). Delete the old `FreeUnitFrames` folder: the addon says so at login if it is still there. Settings made under the old name are not carried over.
- A new emblem: a pug in the compass ring.

## v0.2.0

- A new name: Pug Unit Frames. It was Free Unit Frames, a name that turned out to be in use already. A pug is a small dog, and a PUG is a pick-up group. It is a homage to PitBull Unit Frames, which has not come to Forever, and it is not that project.
- The addon's folder is now `PugUnitFrames` and its command `/pug` (also `/puf` and `/pugunitframes`). Delete the old `FreeUnitFrames` folder: the addon says so at login if it is still there. Settings made under the old name are not carried over.
- A new emblem: a pug in the compass ring.

Fixed:

- With a controller, the menu the game opens on your target (inspect, trade, follow) closed the moment it opened. The game opens it as the menu of its own target frame, which this addon used to hide, and a menu closes when the frame it belongs to is not on screen. That frame is now set aside unseen instead of hidden, and the game shows it with your target as it always did.
- A shaman's totem slots could light up empty in a fight, and a totem whose time had run out could stay drawn until the fight ended. In a fight the game calls a slot taken for every element you have learnt; a slot is now drawn by the time left on it.
- A click on a frame with Shift, Ctrl or Alt held did nothing. It now targets, as a plain click does. A click you have bound to a spell, in the game's click casting or in an addon such as Clique, is cast as bound.
- The game's ping key did nothing with the mouse over a frame. It now pings whoever the frame shows.
- A cast bar could stay up for good when the game never said the cast had ended (a party member's Aimed Shot is the known case). A bar on show is now looked at again a few times a second and goes when its time is up.
- "The font could not be loaded" could be reported at login when the game was only slow to have the file ready. It is tried again a few times first, and the frames change to it when it arrives.
- The count of stacks on an icon could not be read on a bright icon. It is outlined now, whatever the text setting.
- The power number followed the bar in steps, and a combo point showed a moment late. Both now move with every tick on the frames you watch closely.
- A rare creature had no mark beside its level: it is now "23R", and "23R+" when it is elite as well.
- Someone else's kill was only grey when the bar was coloured by class or by friend and foe. It is grey however the bar is coloured.
